newsitem.title: USA: Nissan pulls franchise from USA dealer.
newsitem.headline: Nissan pulls franchise from USA dealer.

text.p: Nissan Motor Corp USA, a unit of Japanese automaker Nissan Motor Co Ltd, canceled its franchise agreement with a Virginia car dealership after the owner allegedly used a racial slur to describe a black worker, The Washington Post reported on Friday.
Representatives from Nissan USA were not available for comment.

According to the paper, the automaker delivered a termination letter to Bob Crumpler, the owner of Nissan dealerships in Newport News and Portsmouth, Va. who was secretly videotaped making the offensive remark.
A man who works at the dealership taped Crumpler referring to a black worker at the Newport News location as a "nigger," the newspaper said. A local television station aired the tape.
"As soon as we heard about this tape, we got a copy of the transcript and our management reviewed it and took swift action," the paper quoted a Nissan spokesman.

The action follows two other high-profile, corporate race discrimination cases: three African-American women sued HFS Inc unit Avis Rent-a-Car and one of its franchise owners for allegedly denying to rent to them; and oil company Texaco Inc recently settled a suit for $176 million after top executives were caught on audiotape making derogatory racial remarks and plotting to destroy evidence.
